title: What Queue really does, and where your picture went
hook: Follow one press of Queue from the editor to a file on disk: what is sent, what waits, what history keeps, and how the file gets its name.

verified.claim: The queue is a heap ordered by number, and front=true makes the number negative.
History is a plain dictionary in memory, capped near 10000 entries, and main.py strips the sixth field of a queue item before storing it.
Prefix to subfolder, name and counter, including the refusal to leave the output folder and a %date% token staying literal on the server.
Running the same graph twice wrote one file and returned the same output record both times. Changing the colour wrote a second.
verified.ref: execution.py:PromptExecutor with the classic cache, on graph a_save_preview

verified.claim: PreviewImage wrote to the temp folder with the record type temp. A batch of two took two counter values.
The temp folder is removed at startup when the assets system is off, and that system is off unless --enable-assets is given.
The editor sends client_id, prompt and extra_data with extra_pnginfo.workflow, and turns %date:...% into text before sending.
verified.ref: ComfyUI front end main branch, packages/api-client/src/ComfyApi.ts and src/extensions/core/saveImageExtraOutput.ts, fetched 2026-11-01

unchecked: We read the front-end code on its main branch and did not press Queue by hand in a browser for this lesson, so what the buttons and side panels look like is left out.
With --enable-assets the temp folder is handled differently, and we did not read how far that goes.
